capture.source: production result store, read-only as the task owner

limitations: Runtime and memory grow rapidly with alignment width because the fitted coupling tensor is quadratic in positions and amino-acid states.

Coupling strength is statistical dependence extracted from the fitted model; it is not by itself proof of a physical contact, causal interaction, or functional coupling, and the contact-oriented reading is a downstream use of these scores.

The reported Hamiltonian is the model's statistical MRF energy, not a thermodynamic free energy. The source paper's stability correlations are empirical and system-specific and say nothing about any particular run.

method.name: GREMLIN_LH Potts model
method.output_summary: Model fields and couplings, raw and APC score matrices, ranked residue pairs, sequence scores, and fit provenance.
method.summary: Fit a regularized Potts model and residue-coupling landscape from a supplied protein MSA.

views.description: Frobenius norms of the fitted pairwise couplings. These are statistical dependencies in the fitted model, not proof of a physical contact; the contact-oriented reading is a downstream use of the scores.
views.title: Coupling strength (raw Frobenius)

views.description: The same coupling norms after average-product correction, shown for comparison. PRX Life reports that for LH weights in its tuned range the raw matrix converges toward this corrected one, so the correction is a post-correction reference rather than the primary object; that is the paper's asymptotic benchmark result, not a property of any particular run.
views.title: Coupling strength (average-product corrected)

views.description: Upper-triangle residue pairs ordered by APC-corrected coupling strength, with the raw score alongside. Statistical dependence, not a physical contact claim.
